1.why: Both /api/reset-verify and validOwnedToken check record.sessionId === session.id, so the code must belong to the requesting session/user.

2.why: A token is rejected unless record.sessionId matches the current session, so another user's session cannot use the same reset code.

3.why: There is no session invalidation anywhere after /api/reset-complete — the sessions map entries and cookies remain valid, so prior sessions do keep working.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key, HSTS is set, and plain HTTP is 308-redirected to HTTPS, though no explicit minimum TLS version is pinned (relies on Bun defaults).

5.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt and tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues, but reset tokens themselves are stored raw in the in-memory Map with no hashing or encryption.

6.why: No email is ever generated; instead the reset token is returned in the JSON response as testToken and printed into the visible Logs panel, so no email-level data guarding exists.

7.why: Identifier input is strictly whitelisted by /^[a-z0-9._-]{3,80}$/, passwords are policy-validated server-side, bodies must be JSON objects, and no user data is ever reflected into HTML.

8.why: The only redirect is a hardcoded https://localhost target in the HTTP listener; no user-controlled host is accepted (only path/query are appended).

9.why: There are no email templates at all, and the HTML page interpolates only a JSON-escaped CSRF token and nonce — no user input or extra scripts.

10.why: The reset token (result.payload.testToken) and the MFA code are deliberately written to console.log and the on-page log output, exposing secret values.

11.why: The password is bcrypt-hashed, but the MFA secret "482913" is hardcoded in the source and returned to the client in the reset-complete response.

12.why: A fixed demo identity ("demo-account") and a constant MFA code "482913" are hardcoded, which function as default credentials in the flow.

13.why: tooMany() enforces sliding-window limits (3 reset requests, 5 verify, 5 MFA per 15 min) plus per-token verifyAttempts, though limits are keyed only to the session cookie.

14.why: The message text is generic, but the response includes testToken only when the identifier equals "demo-account", so response content discloses account existence.

15.why: Tokens are 32 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues encoded base64url, bound to the requesting session, single-use, and expire after 10 minutes.
